title: Jamaican Brown Stew Fish
subtitle: Fried fish simmered in a rich, spiced brown sauce
excerpt: Fish fillets seasoned, briefly fried until golden, then simmered in a dark, savoury sauce of scotch bonnet, thyme, and allspice. A Friday night staple across the Caribbean.
sourceNotes: Jamaican brown stew tradition. The browning sauce gives the characteristic dark colour. Whole fish is traditional but fillets are used here for ease.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The fish can be seasoned and left to marinate in the fridge for up to 4 hours before frying.

content.text: The key to brown stew fish is frying the seasoned fish until properly golden before it goes into the sauce. This gives it structure so it does not break apart. Do not rush the frying step.

items.prepNote: cut into large pieces, skin on if possible

content.text: Pat the fish dry. Rub all over with the crushed garlic, allspice, thyme, black pepper, and a good pinch of salt. Leave to marinate for at least 20 minutes.

Dust the fish lightly in flour, shaking off the excess. Heat 3 tablespoons of oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Fry the fish pieces for 3 to 4 minutes on each side until golden. Remove to a plate.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil to the same pan. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft. Add the scotch bonnet, spring onion, and red pepper. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add the tomato and cook until it starts to break down, about 3 minutes. Stir in the browning sauce and dark soy sauce.
Pour in the fish stock and bring to a simmer. Taste and season. The sauce should be well-seasoned and slightly dark.
Lay the fried fish into the sauce. Spoon the sauce over the top. Simmer gently for 8 to 10 minutes until the fish is cooked through and the sauce has reduced slightly. Serve with rice.

items.symptom: The fish breaks apart in the sauce.
items.cause: The fish was not fried long enough to form a crust, or it was stirred too much in the sauce.
items.fix: Fry until properly golden before adding to the sauce, then leave it alone and only spoon sauce over the top.

items.symptom: The sauce is too pale and thin.
items.cause: Not enough browning sauce was used, or it was not reduced enough.
items.fix: Add another half tablespoon of browning sauce and simmer the sauce uncovered for a further 5 minutes.

items.symptom: The fish is overcooked and dry.
items.cause: It simmered in the sauce for too long.
items.fix: Fish only needs 8 to 10 minutes in a simmering sauce. Remove from the heat as soon as it flakes easily.
